# Chapter Thirteen: Si Vis Pacem, Para Bellum

Sic Pac Parabellum

Standing over the craftsman’s table as the light from the furnace glowed bright in the large space, the syncopated sound of multiple master smiths rang out through the room as ancient recipes not used since the Mage Wars generations before began to take shape and molten metal folded and refolded with crystal resin, carbon and a few other ingredients began to form long slender blades. Marcus looked on and nodding in approval as the designs he had painstakingly worked over began to come to life.

Master Leatherworkers cut and sewed integrating silver and crystal into a design Marcus had pulled from the vast sets of memories given to him. He was now a runic mage, something that had not walked this earth for generations, though his knowledge was limited the smiths and workers regaled him with legends and tall tales of runic mages of old, who could fly through the air and throw buildings. Marcus had smiled at these tales but he didn’t put much stock into them, integrated into his skin was the glowing blue runes of power that he could feel power as it continuously flowed through them, causing the runes to pulse as if they had a life and a heartbeat of its own.

Marcus had tested his new ability to harness the power as a runic mage and his ability to consume and direct energy was beyond anything he could have imagined. He now understood how the Seer, despite his imperfect implementation of this same process had been able to so easily overpower him. He had awoken on this world a powerful mage, but the Silvan’s had done something he didn’t think was possible, they had made him damn near invincible.

“Master Mage, your blades are complete” a gently voice said breaking him from his thoughts as he turned to see the tall stout Silvan Master Smith, her white hair tied back into a tight ponytail. When he had requested the best craftsman from Durass he had sent him two Master Smiths whose skill was unequaled. They had completed the components of the weapon and the parts for the armor and they had come out perfect.

With a smile Macrcus held out his hands and the Master Smith placed two long slender blades into them, they were breathtaking he thought looking them over as he moved to the table where he had laid out all of the components they had created. Reaching into the well of new knowledge that now filled his head Marcus began working through the runes he would need in his head. “Master Mage, I noticed the odd layering of runes, may I ask what they do?” the Master Smith asked as she looked down at the components littering the table. Marcus smiled “It’s a tequnique few have used Master Smith, it allows for layering of the spells needed for defense and offense, intertwining them in a way that they feed off of each other. It’s a tequnique that was used by the first people, but not since.” He finished but what Marcus had left out was that no one had been able to use it because the ability to see power as it flowed allowing him a closer relationship with his gift had not been seen since the days his fellow ARC members had taken back the earth after the devastation that had erased humanity from the planet.

“He is being modest, its much more then that, those spells are beyond even the knowledge of our rune masters” came a voice from the entrance to the room that now held the stations needed to build the weapons and armor the Mage needed. Marcus turned towards the door to see General Durass leaning against it smiling as he looked over the table at the pieces laying there. “I take it, they have given you everything you need?” he asked. Durass had been there when Marcus had drawn up the plans, he had reviewed them with him excited and in awe at the engineering behind them though Marcus could not take any credit for it, the plans were part of the gift the ancient Silvan Mage had given him. “They have, I was about to start scribing them, would you like to stay and watch?” Marcus ask knowing the man would decline, watching someone inscribe objects unless you could watch the power evolve and flow was tant amount to watching paint dry.

As suspected Durass declined with a shake of his head. “However, before you do, would you join me for lunch?” he asked and something about the request made Marcus narrow his eyes and take a good look at the man, there was worry in his eyes. He has news and I am not going to like it Marcus thought nodding his head accepting the offer.

Leaving the room as the Smiths and Crafters continued there work the two crossed the hall and entered a small private room that had already been setup with a table and chairs. The room, like the rest of the underground complex used by the Silvan Mages was completely made of crystal giving an erie feeling of seeing yourself over and over again while looking at a wall, similar to the effect of laying mirrors in front and behind you. It was enough to give a person vertigo Marcus throught taking a seat in one of the padded dark wood chairs that had been provided.

It was only a moment before waiters appeared carrying various trays of food and before Marcus knew it a vast spread appeared before them. Durass motioned for him to dig in and he quickly ablidged the General. He had not realized just how hungry he was until that moment and he began carving off pieces of the large roasted bird and scooping heaps of a steamed yellow vegetable onto his place. “So, you didn’t just come down to take me on a date I take it” Marcus said illiciting a small smile from the general, but one that quickly disappeared.

“No, I wanted to update you there are things in motion you need to know about, also there has been an incident” he said, and Marcus watched as the man winced as the words left his mouth. “What sort of incident?” he asked leaning in the food temporarily forgotten. Durass looked away studying the wall for a moment and then with a sigh he spoke. “LowLanders were attacked by screamers, they seemed to know where they moved to and once they were settled, a small number of them attacked, some people died but most are okay” he said and Marcus’s eyes narrowed “weren’t they in camps protected by your people” he asked and Durass shook his head. “No, we knew they would be in the path of an army and the leader a holy man, came up with a solution to move them out of danger, taking up in an old Warden complex, they headed over a week ago and we just got word of the attack, apparently from what I can ascertain of the motives, they were to be made an example of, but we are not sure” the General said.

Marcus’s eyes narrowed “But that’s not all of it is it?” he asked knowing the information was bad, but the General wouldn’t have invited him to lunch, unless there was more. Durass sighed shaking his head “please understand my people are scared, they are not themselves..” he started and then stopped, shaking his head and then started again “The council will meet in the morning, they are going to vote on wether to excile the lowlanders, the wardens everyone who isn’t a Silvan out of the Northern Dominance, they feel its making the situation worse and might allow them the ability to negotiate with the Empress” he said and before Marcus could speak he held up his hand. “The Empress’s army is already marching, they don’t understand this means she will invade reguardless, I need you to talk to the council Marcus, your voice will carry weight” he said, and the mage sat back reguarding the old General. “General Durass, what sway could I possibly have over your people, I have been hidden away down here, hell I haven’t even seen my friends much less many of your people” Marcus said and again Durass winced. “There was a reason for that, among my people there is a legend, one that pertains to your situation and word has gotten around, you have been kept separate for your protection and frankly to keep you out of the public eye, plus you were needed here and what you needed was here” Durass answered.

Marcus reguarded the general for a moment trying to form words for a problem he never imagined he would have to deal with “What kind of legend?” the Mage finally asked and the General looked embarrassed and with a breath began to speak but doing his best not to make eye contact with Marcus “There is a story of one of the fallen who will arrive when he is most needed, he will be a powerful mage and lead all of our people into the next age” he said “There is more and its very detailed but suffice it to say, the story of your arrival and the fact the Empress is hunting you has inspired people to believe you are this person” he finished and Marcus stared unbelieving at the other man. “You do understand that your first ones were not sent here by gods and my late arrival probably had a lot more to do with a software glitch then anything else” he said exasperated. Durass looked at him curiously “Software?” he finally asked, and Marcus shook his head, he had forgotten for a moment who he was talking to “Machinery broke down” he finally chose as the closest thing he could think to associate it with. Durass nodded “I understand and I also know people are desperate and scared and sometimes when they are, they cling to irrational hope Marcus, but because of that it allows you leverage with our council, will you please speak to them, argue for the lowlanders to remain” he finally asked his voice wasn’t quite pleading but the sentiment was there.

Marcus stared at the old General for the moment “Yes General I will, because to turn them away would be tant amount to murder and I can’t condone that” he finished and watched as the General slumped with relief. Marcus thought for a moment and then finally decided there really would never be a good time to ask “General, what do you know of your origins, I mean how it is your people ended up so different from the low landers” he asked the General, to his credit Durass smiled humorously “I do know that the first ones, a group of them, left behind those like them and came north. They were experts in manipulating aspects of the body and set to work making a new breed of man, one who was more acclimated to there environment, because of the gifts given to the first ones, they studied and researched using the gift to help these changes along, that is how we came to be and the other races as well” Durass finished and Marcus perked up “the other races?” he asked he had not known there were others who had been changed and his mind tried to imagine what other races there could be. Durass smiled again “Some of our animals were augmented and other groups of people continued north, settling in various areas and the first went to work ensuring that they were acclimated to the environment” he finished waving his hand. It appeared that was all Marcus was going to get out of him on the subject, so he concentrated on eating and they spent the rest of the lunch in a companionable silence.

After lunch Marcus returned to his craft table and looked over the armor and components, with a sigh he reached into a drawer and extracted a set of fine tools, etching tools used by the mages to engrave. Marcus closed his eyes, taking a breath he opened them, concentrating on one of the shafts of the mage staff, his eyes began to glow as runic script began to superimpose itself over the object allowing him to mentally see a pattern. With that Marcus gently picked up one of the diamond bit tools and began to etch into the shaft of the weapon. It took many long hours before the entire staff was contoured with runic etchings, once that was complete he pulled a small bowl and a few powered and liquid ingredients and began to mix them together it didn’t take long to complete the liquid and once done he concentrated on it a line of the liquid lifting out of the bowl, it began to run through the indent engraved into the shaft filling it, as it complete a rune and began to flow to the next one, Marcus willed heat into it hardening the rune and then the connector. He did this over the next hour and once he was done, he held up the completed shaft, willing a small amount of power through it and watching as the single runic script over the hilt pulsed with energy.

It was almost dawn when he laid down the last piece on the table, every component covered with runic script. Marcus looked over the pieces laying out in front of him and began picking up pieces from a memory he didn’t own and assembling them. By the time everything was assembled and laid out on the table it was almost time to meet the council. Taking off the cloth shirt and pants he pulled on the black leather pants, the padding giving it the look of motorcycle pants he had owned when he was a teenage, he thought with a smile.

The tall boots were next, the hard souls and multiple buckles took a few minutes to close but once done he walked around the room realizing they had been made to the exact size of his feet and he smiled approvingly. The shirt was next, it was cotton and laced up the front and, on the sleeves, the high neck almost giving it a clerical look as he laced it up and checked the fit. The jacket was next picking it up off of the table he had not realized quite how heavy it was. He held it out and admired the floor length black leather coat with silver buckles, the neck also high again giving it almost an asian look he thought pulling it on and checking the fit. He buttoned up the coat and pulled on the gloves, the knuckles of the black gloves had been reinforced under the leather with metal giving him a hidden advantage in hand to hand combat. There was no focus rune on the glove as he now had one embedded into his skin. He stretched out and moved around, appreciating the fit of the outfit.

Finally, he picked up the obsidian staff, at only three feet long it looked more like a stick he thought, the ends capped with silver and crystal on each end was a carved focus rune, allowing him to use them like thick wands should he need to. He twisted the shafts and the staff lengthened to five feet. Spinning it he felt the weight and balance and again smiled at the ingenuity of the modified design. He shortened the staff back to the original size and then twisted the shafts putting them apart so now he held two foot and a half sticks, the ends could be used to project energy giving him a distance edge in mage to mage combat. He flipped a button and long slender run engraved blades shot out of the other ends, giving him two bladed weapons should he need it.

He retracted the blades and combined the two shafts. On his side was a holster of sorts for the weapon, in fact it was the only weapon he carried. The orginal design had been modified from the weapon he had seen both Maelen and the Seer carry. The craftsmen had wanted to build him the traditional sword of a Runic Mage, but he had begged off, choosing this instead.

He moved over to the smooth crystal wall and unfolded the cowl on the coat, putting it up he admired himself. The outfit was completely black however the runic script covering every inch of every item he wore was just enough of a color difference to be noticeable. “You are a bad mother fucker” be breathed smiling at himself. He felt dangerous, mysterious it was like when you put on an expensive suit for the first time, or the uniform of the military or police it gave you a feeling of pride and worth. It was like that he thought still admiring the outfit, it was his armor in combat and his protection against those who would judge him he thought.

“I have never seen the armor of a Runic Mage, but I had heard the tales, I have to say seeing it in person, its quite the sight” Durass said and Marcus could hear the awe in the man’s voice. It must be quite a sight he thought smiling under his cowl “Is it time?” he asked and the General nodded. The two walked over to the spiral staircase that led back up to Durass’s study, Marcus took one last look around he wasn’t sure why be he thought this might be the last time he would see the place. The ancient mage was nowhere to be seen and he felt a pang of regret not being able to thank him.

The two ascended the stairs coming back into the General’s house. “Once we go in there, you will have to speak, I have been censured but my opinion is well known” he said and Marcus shot a glance at him “Censured?” he asked and Durass shot him a weak smile, one of the costs of gaining you admittance to talk to the council, there were some who were dead set against it.” He finished and motioning to Marcus he led the way out of the room and towards the front of the house.

Durass opened the door and stepped outside, Marcus followed close behind squinting as it took a moment for his eyes to adjust to the light, how long had he been down there he wondered as his vision returned and his eyes widened, looking out over the street it was packed with people all turned towards the General’s porch as everyone pushed one another to get a view of Marcus. “I warned you” Durass said nodding to soldiers standing to either side of his gate, they began to push and shove people out of the way, though even the shoving was gentle Marcus noticed as Durass began to walk forward and Marcus followed, his cowl up he hid his face from the assault of adjulation certainly these people couldn’t believe in a legend he thought or that they would believe he was some kind of chosen figure his mind continued as people reached out, dragging their hands over his armor, trying to touch him.

Though the streets were packed and soldiers had to open the way, the people were orderly, he half expected to be mowed down by a wave of people pushing back against the soldiers, but they aloud themselves to be moved and a path opened as the two walked towards the large government building. Aproaching Marcus heard the yells from the Silvan’s, desperate calls of “Save Us” or “Help Us” or “Defend Us” as they continued to walk.

Marcus did not know how to answer, but wanted to explain he wasn’t a legend or a mythic figure but a man, one with fears and doubts like any other but he did not know how to talk to these people, not in a way that they would listen, so he continued forward, his head hidden under the cowl as they made the steps and quickly ascended them. The doors opened and both men stepped inside. As Marcus entered, he turned just in time to not get bowled over as Dara flung herself into his arms.

“Marcus, we were so worried, are you okay?” she asked, pulling away and looking him over, he couldn’t help but smile at her overt show of worry and affection Master Patrice stood just behind her smiling and shaking her head “Its good to see you in one piece Marcus, Durass assured us you were ok, but Dara was worried sick” She finished and he nodded to her, extracting himself from Dara long enough to give Patrice a hug as well. “It is so good to see you two, there is a lot to tell you, but right now I need to see the council” he said and both women sobered up. “Marcus, they are threatening to send us back across the border, despite the army marching here right now, we would be put directly into there path, they might as well just kill us now” Patrice said bitterly. “The General would never allow that” came a booming voice from his left and Marcus turned to see a large man in Wardens dress, shadowed by an attractive woman, though standing next to him she looked positively tiny. “Uri knows me too well” Durass said smiling as he walked over and embraced the large man.

“Master Mage Marcus Gavin, this is Master Adjucator Uri Ammital and his protégé Warden Corliss Bor” The General said and Marcus stepped over, grasping the man’s forearm “It is good to meet you Uri” and then he turned to the woman and cocked his head “Bor?” he asked and she almost blushed as she nodded. “The only daughter of Galen Bor” she almost whispered and then before Marcus could speak “We weren’t close, at all” and grasped his forearm “It is good to meet you Marcus, though I was chasing you for a while for Galen, util you vanished south of Turen” she said and smiled. Galen cocked his head he had no idea anyone had been hunting his and Maelen’s trail but damn if the old man hadn’t been cunning as well as smart if he managed to lose a Master Warden.

Marcus nodded to her “Well I am very glad you did lose me Warden, now if you two don’t mind I am going to try and talk some sense into the council if I can” he said sounding much more confident then he felt. What the hell do I know about speaking to anyone he thought taking a breath, what the hell can I say to them I am no politician or world leader, Uri or Durass would be far better at this then I would he continued.

He stepped forward trying to hide his nervousness as he stood before the large double doors, the guards motioning him to pause and he did. Laying back the cowl he closed his eyes and mentally braced himself trying to push down the fear trying to well up inside.

The hall stood quiet as Marcus continued to stand upon the threshold of the council’s chambers, the soldiers waiting for orders to allow him admittance. Standing there his mind raced trying to figure out what he would say, how he would say it, knowing the entire future of every low lander and warden rested upon his shoulders and he felt powerless… Ironic he thought, he had been transformed into one of the most powerful mages on the planet and yet here he stood feeling helpless and scared. It was almost enough to make him laugh.

An assistant came out of a side entrance, walking casually over to where Marcus stood, he smiled and nodded “They will see you now Master Mage” he whispered as the doors opened and light spilled in highlighting the room. Marcus stepped inside the cavernous area was intimidating as he made his way to the center of a semi circle where twelve people sat upon raised platforms looking down upon him. He pushed down the fear and doubt that threatened to overtake him, doing his best to control his breathing he came to stand in the center of the large room, putting his hands behind his back mostly so no one could see them shake Marcus put a small grin on his face and did his best to look relaxed.

“Master Mage Marcus Gavin, thank you for accepting our summons to appear” an elderly lady said from the center podium her face looked kind but Marcus could see the hard penetrating stare of her eyes, calculating even he thought and woe anyone who thought of her as an old doddering fool he mused bowing slightly to the woman as she finished speaking.

“Thank you for having me, I am unsure of protocol so I apologize if I do not address you properly Madam” he said keeping his face relaxed and the small smile in place despite the nervous energy that now exploded in his body. The woman smiled approvingly “House Chair Master Mage, you may refer to me as Madam or Madam Chairperson” she corrected and again Marcus slightly bowed “Of Course Madam Chairperson, how may I be of service today” Marcus queried and there were whispered up and down the line of desks he couldn’t hear what exactly they were saying but whatever it was irritated the Chair and she banged a metal ball against her table. “Everyone will have time to ask pertinent questions to the Master Mager” she stated adding emphasis to pertitent which Marcus found interesting.

“Now, Master Mage the reason we are here is to decide wether to allow all Low Landers the ability to stay within our borders, or to expel them in an effort to stave off the impending attack. There are some here who believe by expelling the LowLanders and the Wardens we will show the Empress we are not a threat nor do we want to get involved in the conflict, there are others who think that if the Empress wished to talk, she would have done so already and expelling refugees back across the border only to have them slaughtered would be a stain on our honor” she finished and judging by the way she had said that Marcus could guess which side she was on. In fact, as he looked up and down the row of desks, he could see the averted gazes, hostile looks or approving nods. Surprisingly there were a lot more of those who seemed to warm to the idea of expelling Marcus thought doing a quick count in his head. If they voted now, he judged it would be close, so there was still hope at least he mused.

Marcus nodded and remembered his conversation with Rogan, the Seer something he had said, something about mundanes and then the words came to him and he began to speak.

“Governors, I have spoken to one of the Empress’s chosen, I am even hunted by her, wanted for some dark purpose. This is a woman who has turned her entire kingdom inside out based on the believe that the entire world should be under one rule and that rule should be by the will of Mages, mundanes only exist according to her doctrine to serve the Mages. Everyone to her is a slave, she has proven this with her action and her disreguard for life, The Empress has broken every tenant, pact or promise that the crown has made.” Marcus began, looking over the Govenors gathered before him and seeing the different reactions, but despite some of the hostile looks everyone was listening he thought.

“She has not reached out and opened dialog, instead the Empress has marched her army north do you honestly think if you give up her subjects, she will see this as anything other then a sign of weakness and fear spurning her armies here faster?” Marcus asked and could see some of them wince oh so they hadn’t thought of it like that he mused hiding a smile. “Throwing out those who would only be slaughtered as an example of what happens when you defy the Empress as she attempted to the north with those refugees who left your territory and sought safety will be seen as a weak attempt to stave off the inevitable and an affirmation that she is stronger then you” he finished.

“That’s absolute conjecture, he is not a member of the royal court and has no idea what this Empress thinks” one man, standing his massive belly hung over the table as he bellowed more objections, but the Chair quickly silenced him. “Quiet Kopril, you seem to be more them comfortable telling us what she is thinking and the Master Mage spoke to one of her chosen, which is more then you have” she stated and Marcus could hear the suppressed chuckles up and down the row. “Certainly there has to be some way to reason with her, do we want the bloodshed of our people on our hands without even trying to open a dialog?” came another voice, this one getting more then a few grunts of affirmation. Marcus nodded “That’s a reasonable thought Govenor, have you tried to send a messenger to talk to the Seer’s, you might consider trying that to find out if the Empress would even want to entertain terms before you give away your biggest bargaining chip” Marcus said, he almost winced as he did, where the hell had that come from.

But from wherever in his mind it had flowed it had been the right thing to say, it aloud those that hated the idea a moment to pause and those for it a reason to find out if it would even matter.

Everyone began to whisper to one another until the chair banged the large silver ball quieting them. “Master Mage you speak wisdom beyond that tied to the emotional connection to your low landers and its wisdom I think we can consider, you have given us a few things to think about, would you please wait outside while we deliberate, but please stay close in case we need to call upon you” the chair stated and Marcus bowed deeply “Of Course Madam Chair, I am at your service” he said turning and walking from the room. As soon as the doors closed everyone gathered looked to him “Well, what are they going to do?” Dara asked and Marcus could see everyone leaning in awaiting an answer.

“They aren’t going to kick us out quite yet, if I had to guess, they are going to send a messenger under a flag of truce to see if the Empress will discuss terms” he finished and there was a reserved sigh of relief. “So, we are not quite out of the woods, but also not having to pack our bags just yet” Uri Ammital said smiling at Marcus “Well done Master Mage, well done” he finished clapping Marcus on the back.

The Govenors deliberated for two more hours before the door opened and a tiny woman shuffled out with the aid of a cane, Marcus almost didn’t recognize her, until he saw her eyes “Madam Chair?” he asked confused as to why she would be outside the chambers. Stopping the woman reguarded Marcus for a moment and then smiled “Master Mage, will you accompany me for a walk?” she asked and confused Marcus nodded walking over to the woman and stepping next to her keeping up as she shuffled down a hallway, Marcus in tow.

They were silent for a while, going down one hall, turning and going down yet another. The warm wood coloring and feel of the building putting Marcus at ease, as if the natural wood coloring pleased some primal portion of his brain. “Well thanks to your advice, we are going to send a missive to the army marching at us, we will fly under a banner of truce to see if we can open a dialog” she said smiling up at him. “I wanted to thank you Master Mage, I do not think my ancestors would look kindly upon me throwing innocent people to the wolves so to speak and it wasn’t a decision I was reslishing having to make” he finished and he could see the haunted look in the woman’s eyes as she continued.

“I was the one who approved the low lander refugees request to leave, in fact I did it and breathed a sigh a relief that, that political headache was off of my plate. But then I heard what happened, had I thought with my heart Master Mage there would be many more people alive today” she finished, and Marcus nodded. “You made a decision based on the information you had, you could not have known the Empress would seek them out despite them being out of the way of the army and there objective. Now at least you can find out where you stand before making a decision that will not only affect your conscience but also your country” Marcus concluded, and the old woman stopped looking up at the Mage. “Again, you speak wisdom far beyond your years young one, I for one am glad you do” she said padding Marcus on the arm as they walked back towards the antechamber.

“Master Mage, we are sending a small contingent in the next hour, would you please go and offer any help or advice you can, I don’t expect you to ride out, but having you there” she began and then paused choosing her words “would make a lot of people breathe easier” she finished and smiled up at him. Marcus thought this had something to do with the hero worship outside, but if it helped, he would do it. “Of course, Madam Chair, I would be honored” he concluded and bowed to her as she entered the chamber, the large doors closing behind her.

An hour later Marcus, Dara, Patrice, Durass, Uri and Corliss as well as half of the Govenors and their staff stood in the woodline as six riders on horses flew a white flag as they rode across the field. The soldiers had been on the other side of the clearing since the morning, they had made no move to advance but also had not setup any camps, Marcus didn’t know what they were waiting for and for some reason it was making him nervous as the center of his shoulder blades itched, as if someone had painted a target on it.

“I am surprised they are riding horses General; I would have thought you would want to show your enemy what awaits them” Uri said, and Marcus cocked his head straining to hear the conversation over the rustling of trees. Durass smiled “We decided to keep that for a surprise, besides you Low Landers brought so many horses, why waste them and tire our beasts out” he said. What beasts Marcus wondered as he watched the riders slow as they approached the standing army.

They slowed coming to stand directy in front of two robed figures with there cowls drawn. Marcus tried to get a better look at them but couldn’t, they were Lord Seer’s he knew that much, but would Rogan be here he wondered. After only a moment, one of the robed figures stood on his horse and made a motion with his hand. Everyone gasped in horror as flame engulfed the riders and the horses, the animals died so fast they didn’t even take a step before collapsing. Marcus couldn’t hear the men scream, but he knew what happened when you covered a man in magic flame as he thought back to Orah’s farm and the collectors.

Before anyone could react, a call went up and to Marcus’s horror as he watched a hundred blue energy trails erupted from behind the line of soldiers. “Cannons” Yelled Uri and everyone began to scramble, Marcus turned to the group gaining everyone’s attention by clapping his hands and enhancing it with magic, what it produced was as loud as a thunder clap, everyone jumping but now looking at him “get everyone back to the city, I will cover you” he said evenly and then turned back to the oncoming enemy fire. He stepped just outside of the treeline and looked up as the arcs reached their pinnacle and began to descend on his position.

He watched them for a few moments, the cannons had been loaded and aimed well in advance, as if the enemy knew this is something the Silvan’s would do and that they would have some of there leaders here watching, they had hoped to cut the head of the snake Marcus thought shaking his head as anger welled up in him. “Not today” he said and summoned energy, the runes over his body flowing faster as they accumulated massive amounts of power, his eyes flashed blue as he pushed towards the enemy with his hand and the cannon fire snapped back, the energy trails reversing as the balls returned home to there guns.

He could here the yelling once the soldiers saw the incoming fire and a moment later satisfying explosions over the horizon as they landed among the artillery and the soldiers who manned them. One of the Robed seers rode forward dropping his cowl and Marcus’s blood boiled as Rogan leered at him from across the field. The Seer had the sheer audacity to wave at Marcus and then turn his horse and casually return to the line. Taking a step he felt the anger for this man well up inside him, remembering Maelen and what he had done to him.

Taking another step, he pointed to the Seer “Rogan, I am coming for you” Marcus yelled and even from across the field he could see the man smile. Then from his left he heard the heavy beat of horse hoofs and turned to see four of the Empresss soldiers bearing down on him, two held staves and a net was drawn out between the others. Did they really think to capture him he thought shaking his head? Marcus pushed at the next and realized that he couldn’t move it, thinking quickly he knocked the feet out from under the horses instead, sending them crashing to the ground as there riders spilled and rolled, coming to land directly in front of Marcus.

Panicing the Soldiers got up and began to run across the field, back towards the line. Reaching out he grabbed one with his power and snapped him back to land at his feet, the others he aloud to leave, for now. Marcus summoned power and lifted the man off the ground, levitating him so his face was parallel with Marcus’s “What did Rogan do with the body of the Mage he killed in the village of short shore?” he asked. The man was frantically searching for a way out, Marcus tightened his power around him squeezing the soldier and he could hear him fight for breath. “Answer me” he growled when this was done, Marcus would see Maelen buried with honors he thought.

Then the soldier spoke the shock of his words freezing Marcus in place for a moment. “The mage he captured. He is not buried, Rogan had him taken to the tower, please, please don’t kill me” the soldier stammered. Captured Marcus thought, thinking back to the battle, he had heard the explosions and the screams, but he had never seen a body, instead he had assumed Maelen dead and just left his friend. Guilt welled up in him “Where is this tower” he asked, the soldier shaking his head “I, I can’t I am a dead man if I tell you” he said and Marcus squeezed again, the man began to scream as blood ran from his eyes and ears. “Okay, okay” he said, and Marcus released his grip a little. He told Marcus what he wanted to know begging to be set free. Turning Marcus flung the man back towards his line, he sailed halfway across the field before landing in a bloody heap on the field.

He walked back towards the city with a purpose, Dara and Patrice who had waited for him, refusing to leave with the others scrambled to catch up with his fast pace “What are you going to do?” Dara asked having heard the soldier’s confession. Marcus looked at her for a moment and then face towards the city again “I am going to get him Dara” he said evenly. By the time he reached the city they had caught up with the still agitated and afraid precession of Govenors and the Wardens. Durass saw the look on Marcus’s face and shot Patrice a concerned look “What happened?” he asked and she told him. “Marcus, wait, please” Durass said as he passed the group heading for the stables where the horses the low landers rode in on were.

Marcus kept walking refusing to stop, refusing to talk he was going to save the friend he had abandoned, the friend who had saved him his mind said over and over. General Durass came to stand in front of him, causing Marcus to stop “General, get out of my way” he said dangerously as Durass made a placating gesture “Please, Marcus wait” he began but Marcus was about to push by him when Dara threw herself in front of him “Listen Marcus, for one minute please” she said her eyes pleading and full of tears. Finally, his anger abated, he wasn’t going to push her out of the way he thought sighing and turning towards the General.

“What is it General, if you don’t mind I am going to get my friend, the one who sacrificed himself so we all could live” Marcus said the anger and guilt evident in the tone as he shot a look at both Patrice and Dara, why was everyone trying to stop him he thought and eyed the General expectantly. Durass sighed shaking his head “I understand Marcus, I do, but if you leave here, you abandon everyone. Our mages cannot face off against two seers and Aurtus knows how many damn screamers, it will be a slaughter” he finished his voice sounding defeated as he locked eyes with Marcus, his gaze pleading even moreso then his words. “Dammit, don’t put that on me General” Marcus barked averting his eyes he knew what would happen if he left, looking around he could see the people, the children, but he had to save Maelen, dammit the man had sacrificed himself for them, how could he just leave him to the Empress and her twisted experiments. “General, I cannot leave him there, who knows what the Empress is doing to him” Marcus pleaded, trying to get the man to understand. He didn’t want to abandon them, he didn’t want to let everyone die but he owed Maelen, owed him everything he thought. He could see the defeat in the General’s face, but the man wasn’t done he was just about to launch into another plea when someone said “Ill go get him” and everyone stopped. Looking around Marcus tried to figure out who spoke and then the Warden next to Uri stepped forward her usually tight ponytail had come loose framing her face in the blonde hair as the determined spark in her green eyes shone like a beacon to Marcus “What?” he said not sure he had heard her the first time.

“I understand what its like to owe someone, I know you can’t leave him Master Mage, but I also know that if you leave these people now, they are all dead. So I will go retrieve your friend” she finished and the look on her face challenging him to deny her he was about to protest, about to say it was his job when he looked, his eyes roving over the people standing there, eyes averting as they noticed him looking but not before he could see the hope in their eyes. “Marcus, what would your friend tell you to do?” Uri, his arms crossed over his barrel chest but his eyes kind as he asked the question, there was no malice, just an understanding of his internal conflict.

That was it, Marcus had no fight, Maelen would never forgive him if he sacrificed an entire city to save him he thought and Marcus’s shoulders slumped in defeat “Okay, but I need your word you will save him” he said locking eyes with Corliss as the warden took two steps, coming to stand right in front of him.

“I swear, if he is alive, I will save him and if he is not, I will bring the body back so you may honor him. But know this Master Mage I want your word you will stand with these people to the end and defend them with your life, because if I am not going to be here, then I need to know you will stand in my place” she said her eyes shone fierce determination and it caught Marcus offguard for a moment “I swear warden” he simply said and she nodded. Dara stepped forward “I am going with her; she might need a mage and I owe Maelen too” she finished, and she looked over the gathered crowd daring anyone to tell her no. No one did and with a nod she stepped over to Corliss.

Marcus caught something pass between the old ChairPerson and General Durass, the old woman visibly nodded and Durass stepped forward “Before you go, I think we need to ensure you are outfitted correctly” he said Corliss and Uri both giving him a questioning look as he motioned for them to enter the elevator. Once at the top the entire group followed Durass, he walked down the main Market road but before reaching the turnoff towards his house he turned the opposite direction.

The group walked down another row of what looked like Manufacturing and industrial buildings until they came to stand in front of the only building that truly stood out in the entire city. Where everything in the city was masterfully carved woods, all the way down to the decorative wood tile streets the building in front of them was grey, squat and entirely made of stone. It looked like any of the keeps used by the Messengers in fact Marcus thought cocking his head at the curiousty of a Stone keep in the trees. Durass approached the building and putting his hand near the door power gathered showing a circular dial entirely of magic, he spun it several directions and as Marcus’s eyes roved over the door he watched as the spell runes engraved into the door and the frame lit and began to dim quickly. “A Spell lock” Marcus whispered the word coming from knowledge given to him, after saying the word he understood the basic concept, he had no idea things like that existed he thought.

Walking into the building Durass motioned everyone to enter and then nodded as the Old Woman closed the door, standing there in case someone came in. Durass motioned for everyone to gather and ensured they all could hear him. Clearing his throat, he began to speak. “There are a few things you need to know, one of the things we instill in our soldiers is deception. When they go patrol the boundaires and since LowLanders began to show up, we have concealed our weapons and instead used ones LowLanders would be familiar with” Corliss and Uri looked at him oddly “What are you talking about Durass?” Uri asked almost codly.

“My people never gave up on technology, while yours focused on magic, we continued our innovation” he said and then opened a large crate. Marcus heard the gasp and then looked into the crate, as soon as he says it laying there he smiled “Repeating Rifles, Holy Shit” he said. Durass looked Surprised “Your Right Master Mage” he said and shot Marcus a curious look wondering how he knew that. Corliss and Uri both looked back and forth between the two of them and then finally settled back on the rifle in the box.

“What is that?” she asked and proudly Durass picked it up, this is a Silvan repeating rifle, it holds eight shots once you fire, you cock the level” he said and then pulled the leaver down as Marcus heard the mechanism inside engage “Then you can shoot again” he continued. Marcus eyed the rifle, the design looked like a Henry rifle all the way down to the cocking level, the design had definitely been passed down he thought it looked as if the Silvans had been hiding their innovations in technology.

“Why would you hide this?” Corliss asked amazed at what she saw Durass looked slightly embarrassed but pressed on “Because we knew that if it was found out we had this level of weapons technology, how long before one of the countries attack us to get at it, or send spies or Aurtus forbid assasins, so it was decided our technology would remain hidden until such time as we could no longer do it.” He finished.

Durass pulled a smaller box and fished out a revolver “This is a handgun that holds six shots” he said and handed what looked like an old colt army to Corliss. The Warden was beaming as she examined the gun. Durass pulled out an oblong smooth crystal that same light blue as the rounds the musket’s shot and showed it around. “Our cartridges are smaller, faster and far more accurate” he finished.

Corliss and Uri pulled out two pistols each and one rifle, Durass grabbed two leather satchels full of ammo and handed them each one. The group left and Corliss, Dara set off with Uri who was going to ensure they were supplied and got off okay before he would take his place as leader of the patrols, taking the position that Corliss held. “Warden Corliss” Durass Called as the woman approached he held out a belt with two hand tooled holsters “The belt might require a little adjusting, but the holsters ride low on your outer thighs, according to our ancient texts from the first, its called western style and proves popular now among those who carry these.” He finished Corliss taking the leather bundle “Thank you Durass, this will help” she responded and the General smiled nodding at her.

Durass turned to Marcus “Thank you Master Mage, I know he meant a lot to you, I also know how hard it was to stay, for doing so I think I speak for everyone when I say that” he finished and Marcus waved him off “General, after seeing your people and knowing what the Empress and her Seer’s are capable of, The decision wasn’t that hard to make” he said and Durass smiled. “I do have one more thing, would you join me?” he asked and Marcus

“I need to get back to the council, before they vote to flee further north” she smiled and waved her goodbyes. “I need to get to the infirmary and setup, its going to be busy” Patrice stated, taking Marcus’s arm and sqeezing it “Don’t worry, they will bring Maelen back” she said and he could see the hope in her eyes, but also the joy the whole time he had been wrapped up in him saving Maelen he never even stopped to see how Patrice, his lover was taking it. “I know they will Patrice, had I known he was alive” Marcus began but she cut him off “I know” she said giving him a peck on the cheek and heading towards the hospital.

Durass motioned for Marcus to join him and he headed back towards his house. It took them only minutes to reach the house and once inside Durass directed him into his office, Marcus noticed the long, antique wooden box on his desk, going around the desk Durass moved the box so he could get at the lock, he opened it and looked up at Marcus “I know you only chose the mage staff as a weapon, but I wanted to give you this, as a thank you for standing with us” Durass said gently picking up the object and handing it to Marcus. Looking it over Marcus nodded appreciately at the long sword, it was a one-handed bastard style sword, the pommel was the head of a dragon as black wrappings covered the hilt, the guard was a long silver bar curving into two dragon’s claws. “This is a Runic Mages sword, this one was once carried by a Master Mage of our people who was the last Runic to serve during the Mage Wars, I am giving it to you” Durass said and Marcus looked down, the black sheath was covered with runs as was the blade itself. “General, this is a national treasure, I couldn’t possibly take this” Marcus said motioning to hand it back. Durass stopped him “Marcus, this was never meant to sit in a museum and rot, it was meant to defend” he said. Marcus slightly bowed in appreciation of the gift and then slowly pulled the blade from its sheath, the weight of the blade was perfect and then Marcus pushed power into it, the sigils in the sword lit up to his eyes showing the flow and formation of power, it was not only a sword but a giant focus he thought looking over the blade. Without thinking he pointed the blade at a cup and flick a quick spec of power into it. A moment later the cup jumped off the table embedding itself in the ceiling as it hit at an astonishing speed.

Marcus winced “sorry” he said and Durass shrugged. Marcus put the blade back “They come tomorrow General, we need to prepare” The Mage said and the General nodded.

War was coming to the City in the Trees.
